<subject>Achievements for the First Half of 2025</subject>
<body>
My achievements for the first half of 2025 include the following:

1.    AeroParts Manufacturing Contract Templates -- provided essential legal expertise and intellectual input to overhaul manufacturing contract templates to align closely with the aerospace supply chain agreements.

2.   AeroDynamics Ltd and Insolvency Strategy -- led the legal and supplier quality team across all Kestrel Aerospace divisions in mitigating Kestrel’s financial and compliance exposure. This involved a rapid review of Kestrel’s positions and coordination across divisions to determine the optimal approach to terminate and assess all AeroDynamics Ltd contracts.

3.    Implemented New Document Retention Framework for Falcon Engineering -- spearheaded resolution of critical document retention challenges and rolled out a new policy across company divisions at Kestrel.

4.    Thought Leader on Kestrel Risk Management -- continued advancing legal frameworks for enhanced risk monitoring and reporting across the company. The Kestrel Risk Index and legal risk scoring models are two examples. These policies have been recently deployed in the Bristol manufacturing unit and the Supplier Quality department to better assess and control legal risks.

5.     Developing New Aerospace Components Businesses -- played a key role in supporting new product lines in turbine blades, avionics, composite materials, and structural assemblies by drafting contract forms and innovating legal risk management techniques.

6.     Deal Machine -- involved in complex projects including the Falcon Engine II programme, Bristol Advanced Composites, AeroLink Systems, Skybolt Technologies, and Altair Aerospace.

7.     Management -- continued strengthening a deal-focused legal team that understand the core aerospace manufacturing operations.

8.     New Generation of Master Agreements -- leading efforts with the Aerospace Trade Association to develop a next-generation master contract that would unify terms across all aerospace components, whether physical parts or licensing agreements. This is expected to halve the legal workload.
